notes: Net available time = (shift minutes - break minutes) x 60. Allowance is applied once inside planning SAM, never again here.
Theoretical capacity = available HC x net shift minutes x planned efficiency / planning garment SAM. It ignores precedence, machine and line-balance constraints, so it is not a promise of output.
Daily/period capacity and target achievement use the optimizer's bottleneck-constrained capacity, not the theoretical capacity.
Required HC is a theoretical estimate. Skill, machine, precedence and bottleneck constraints can require more people than this estimate.
HC gap = actual HC - standard HC; positive means excess, negative means shortage.
Attendance is a manual input in the MVP; there is no HR/MES integration.
Optimized HC is the number of stations used by the MILP solution.
Transfer suggestions only include unused workers who are eligible for the bottleneck operation.
Synthetic current-state baseline: first-fit 60s station target, one worker per station, respects skill/machine/precedence. Not an optimizer output.
Bottleneck delta is reported as before - after, so a positive value is an improvement.
Baseline violations are listed but do not block the comparison; a real current-state layout may violate the assumptions of the optimized model.
Downtime events and the summary downtime differ; the summary value is used for total downtime, and the category table shows event-level detail.

Production achievement uses the reported target for the same period. Actual labor efficiency uses planning SAM (allowance applied once), not raw SAM. Downtime percentage uses planned shift minutes, not net available minutes.
